intended_object: A threshold partition of G is a split partition (clique K, independent set I) whose independent vertices have neighbourhoods totally ordered by inclusion. This definition restricts such a partition to the induced subgraph G[s], taking K ∩ s and I ∩ s. Inferred from the docstring and the module doc ("Transport preserves the supplied partition").
explanation:
The definition calls `P.comap` with the subtype embedding s ↪ V. In Mathlib, `G.induce s` is by definition `G.comap (Embedding.subtype s)`, so the types line up.

`SplitPartition.comap` takes the preimages of the clique and independent parts. Along the subtype embedding these are exactly the parts intersected with s, seen as subsets of s. Being a clique, being an independent set, disjointness and covering all carry over to these preimages.

Nestedness of the restricted partition is shown by going through P4-freeness, which passes to induced subgraphs. Since nestedness is a Prop field, the proof route does not affect the data. The data is exactly the original partition restricted to s, which is the standard restriction of a threshold (split) partition to an induced subgraph.

Edge cases behave correctly: if s is empty, both parts are empty. Nothing is too narrow either: V and s are arbitrary, and the operation works for any type and any subset. Mathlib has no notion of threshold or split partitions, so there is no counterpart.
